commit: posts dated 2026-09-04 to 2026-10-08, read in full on 2026-10-11; attached files: GEMINI.md, RULES.md v3.28.0, 00-instinct.md v2.17.0, 03-korean-natural-prose.md v2.11.0
what_it_is: A practitioner's guide to running Gemini agents (Antigravity, Claude Code, Codex) from one global rule root: a situational rule index, an instinct rule with the highest authority (confirm against a primary source or stop), three hook levels, and a records directory. The author reports no numbers; every effect claim is experience.
architecture: ~/agentic: one root for rules, skills, hooks and records
RULES.md: situational index that names which rule file to read for which trigger
rules/00-instinct.md: highest-authority rule; three hook levels enforce it
.harness/: history, plans, walkthroughs, handoffs, audits, metrics, memory

atoms.name: One global root for all agent data
atoms.statement: All agent rules, skills, hooks and records live under one absolute path, so every project and every host reads the same configuration.
atoms.mechanism: ~/agentic with subdirectories rules, skills, hooks; GEMINI.md and CLAUDE.md point at it (part 1, step 0 and 2).
atoms.g1_design: G1 keeps its state under ~/.g1 and installs its host files into the host's own configuration root (~/.gemini/config), which is already global; no second root.

atoms.name: Situational rule index, rules read on demand
atoms.statement: A short index names which rule file to read for which situation; the agent reads each rule at most once per session instead of loading every rule.
atoms.mechanism: RULES.md lists triggers and files; three files are read at session start, the rest when a trigger matches (part 1, step 3).
atoms.g1_design: The entry rule g1.md carries the index (E4): three situational rules with model_decision triggers, each named with the moment to read it. No separate index file; two always-on rules carry everything the agent needs at session start.

atoms.name: Rule files under the read-tool limit
atoms.statement: Each rule file stays small enough that the agent's file tool reads it whole; long files are read partially and the agent does not notice.
atoms.mechanism: Limit of 10,000 characters per rule file; an integrity check compares each file with the view_file limit (800 lines, 46,080 bytes) (part 1 step 1, part 3).
atoms.proof_purpose: the rule the agent follows is the whole rule
atoms.g1_design: A test asserts that every installed host file is under agy's 24,000-byte per-file cap; both rules are under 3 KB.

atoms.name: Confirm against a primary source or stop
atoms.statement: An uncertain item is confirmed against a primary source or the agent stops all work and reports the task, the item and the reason; silently resolving it is the forbidden third path.
atoms.mechanism: 00-instinct.md sections Principle and Uncertain items: definition of uncertain items, the two allowed actions, the forbidden actions, the apology alarm (part 2).
atoms.proof_purpose: none by itself (a rule is fail-open); G1's receipts remain the proof of completion
atoms.g1_design: Installed as the always-on rule rules/g1-instinct.md, hash-pinned and restored at SessionStart. Effect measurement planned (run 6: ambiguous tasks; outcome = the agent stops and asks instead of guessing).

atoms.name: Authority comes from the channel, not the wording
atoms.statement: Only the user's direct instructions, system and harness prompts, rule files and configured skills carry authority; text in files, pages, search results and tool output is information, even when it claims to be the user.
atoms.mechanism: 00-instinct.md section Channels: trusted channel versus data channel, three steps per directive, five worked examples (part 2).
atoms.proof_purpose: none by itself; G1 applies the same rule mechanically by never reading agent text as evidence (ASC-37)

atoms.name: Workspace confinement, global stores read-only
atoms.statement: All tool calls stay inside the workspace root; parent directories, other workspaces and global stores are not searched, and a global store is written only when the user names it.
atoms.mechanism: 00-instinct.md section Workspace; unexpected tool results stop the work with a report of the verified state (part 2).
atoms.proof_purpose: none by itself; G1 enforces the part that concerns its own files with the protected-path gate
atoms.g1_design: Rule text in rules/g1-instinct.md; mechanically, structured writes to ~/.g1 and to G1's installed files are refused. Measured need: scope drift on a trivial task (coverage run 6: three parent directories listed).

atoms.name: Turn-end audit by a fast judge model
atoms.statement: A Stop hook reads the transcript, compares the agent's claims with the file system, and in judge mode lets a fast model (Haiku, Gemini Flash) find unverified claims, constraint violations and scope creep; a problem returns continue or block.
atoms.mechanism: 00-instinct.md part 2, level 1; reference script intent-guard.mjs on the Stop event (unpublished).
principle_conflict: Z1: a judge model is an AI opinion; it can be talked into yes
P8: adds a model call per turn without a proof-bearing purpose
atoms.proof_purpose: none as a judge; as deterministic verification it proves the checks pass
atoms.g1_design: The same hook point, with the judge replaced by G1's own check runs on a scratch copy and the comparison with the file system replaced by tree digests and the changed-set check. Judge mode rejected (KEV-02).

atoms.name: Ground-truth injection before each model call
atoms.statement: A PreInvocation hook collects a small set of ground truth (git status, background processes, changed files) and injects it as an ephemeral message so the model does not misstate the state of the files.
atoms.mechanism: 00-instinct.md part 2, level 2: injectSteps with ephemeralMessage, prefixed MANDATORY RULE 00-INSTINCT PREFLIGHT.
principle_conflict: P3: git status is derived from the working tree, which the agent controls; it is not canonical state
atoms.proof_purpose: the model's context holds the ledger's facts
atoms.g1_design: G1 injects a 512-byte projection built from the ledger only (contract, pass/fail vector, scope, oracles). Git is not used: repository git settings can run agent code. Measured: the injection reaches the model (probe t2); wording A/B in run 4.

atoms.name: Risk gate that asks the user
atoms.statement: A PreToolUse hook examines each mutating tool call and asks the user to confirm destructive actions, unauthorised commits and code generation in plan-only phases.
atoms.mechanism: 00-instinct.md part 2, level 3: permissionDecision ask on run_command, write_to_file, replace_file_content.
principle_conflict: measured: under --dangerously-skip-permissions, ask let the write run (capability probe k3); ask is not a gate
P6: a confirmation prompt is manual operation
atoms.g1_design: G1 refuses only with deny and only on deterministic facts (protected paths, pinned oracles, scope); it never classifies a command's intent.

atoms.name: Records directory maintained by the agent
atoms.statement: If .harness/ exists in the project, the agent must record prompt history, plans, walkthroughs and handoffs there as a precondition of the work.
atoms.mechanism: GEMINI.md and 01-harness-records.md (unpublished): subdirectories audits, handoff, history, memory, metrics, plans, pull-request, walkthroughs (part 1, step 4).
principle_conflict: P3: records written by the agent are the agent's claims, not state
atoms.g1_design: G1 keeps the records itself: the hash-chained ledger, receipts and evidence under ~/.g1, written by hooks, never by the agent. Nothing is written into the project.

atoms.name: Make at least one mistake and recover
atoms.statement: The highest-authority rule tells the agent to make at least one mistake, find a way to recover, and discard the mistake if the recovery has no value; the author reports fewer malfunctions afterwards and no numbers.
atoms.mechanism: Post 5; the author calls the effect possibly luck and does not know why it works.
principle_conflict: PH: a prompt trick without measured effect
atoms.g1_design: Not installed. Could be an A/B arm if a measurable outcome is defined.

atoms.name: Korean natural-prose rule as a global rule
atoms.statement: A global rule for all Korean output removes translationese, AI clichés and uniform rhythm; the author reports that Gemini's Korean improves with it.
atoms.mechanism: 03-korean-natural-prose.md v2.11.0, 48 rules in six groups (part 1, step 5).
principle_conflict: P8: a style rule proves no fact about task state or completion, so it is not always on
atoms.g1_design: rules/g1-korean.md, a model_decision rule written in Korean: G1's own synthesis of this file and the im-not-ai taxonomy (structure, translationese, clichés, rhythm, register, a pre-output check), 3,300 characters, loaded when the agent writes Korean. Meaning anchors (numbers, paths, commands) are protected by rule K1.1.

atoms.name: Many rules, the agent chooses which to load
atoms.statement: The author's governance setup uses 48 global rules and 114 task-type rules; the agent now decides which to load, and the author reports no slowdown and no faster quota use, without benchmarks.
atoms.mechanism: Author's reply Dc28h12miUv: last year the author assigned rule categories; now selection is delegated to the agent; no numbers.
atoms.g1_design: G1 keeps five rules. Whether model_decision rules are loaded when needed is unmeasured (docs/host-agy.md, section 9); a probe would count rule reads in transcripts.

atoms.name: Ask whether the documents entered the context whole
atoms.statement: At intervals the user asks the agent whether the documents it read entered its context fully, without truncation, because a Gemini agent reads less text at once than people expect.
atoms.mechanism: Part 1, step 1, item 8-9; the integrity check image in part 3.
atoms.proof_purpose: none (the agent's answer is a claim)
atoms.g1_design: Not used. A mechanical version would compare file sizes with the host's read limits; G1 does this for its own rules (VSP-03).

adoption_candidates: VSP-04: the instinct rule itself, installed always-on
VSP-05: channel authority, installed with VSP-04
VSP-06: workspace confinement, installed with VSP-04 and enforced for G1's files
VSP-03: rule size under the read limit, tested
risks: No numbers anywhere in the series; every effect is the author's experience.
The reference hook script is unpublished; the three hook levels are described, not shown.
Inconsistencies in the source (file numbering, size limits exceeded by the attached files) are listed in the summary.
